_doc: Service-manager automation tuning (#310, parent #297). The decision-function knobs the on-staff service manager uses once its `shop_throughput` clears each function's gate in tunables.json#managerGates.serviceManager.actThresholds. Mirrors data/sourcing.json (channel-desk M6) — gate thresholds live in tunables, the function tuning lives here. All magnitudes are placeholders pending the S14 calibration pass (#286).

par._doc: Demand-driven par tuning. The SM sets each parts category's target/reorderPoint off its trailing intake demand (the ServiceInsights window count). target = max(minTarget, ceil(demand x targetCoverDays)); reorderPoint = max(minReorderPoint, ceil(demand x reorderCoverDays)), capped at target.

posture._doc: Reputation-driven pricing posture. A strong-reputation shop sustains a premium labor/markup posture without driving owners away; a weak one stays competitive to protect retention. posture = lerp(minPosture, maxPosture, clamp01((reputation - floor)/(ceil - floor))).

marketing._doc: Base-health / over-stock-driven marketing. The SM runs the retention arm when forward churn pressure is high (at-risk share over trigger, or churn rising), and aims the conquest arm at the most over-stocked parts category to manufacture demand that clears dead capital (onHand/demand over trigger).

capacity._doc: Capacity-aware rush balancing. Once the capacity function is automated the SM makes the rush-vs-walk call capacity-aware — it only rush-orders a parts miss while the shop has slack (live utilization below the ceiling), otherwise it walks the job rather than overcommit a slammed bay/advisor floor.
